sentences.text: 1 Present miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act has been filed assailing the award dated 22.11.2010 passed by Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 2/2009 filed by the appellants for grant of compensation on account of death of deceased Lokendra Singh in a road traffic accident occurred on 21.10.2002 involving offending vehicle Jeep bearing registration No. MP09-H-4434.

entities.text: Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per claimants, at the time of accident, respondent No. 1 was the owner and respondent No. 2 was the driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No. 1 filed his written statement and denied the allegations made in the claim petition and further stated that he had sold the offending vehicle Jeep to Raghuraj on 02.9.1995.

Later,
Raghuraj sold the Jeep to Ramsiya on 31.10.1995 and prayed that as he was not the owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident, therefore, he is not liable to pay the compensation.
Respondent No. 2 remained absent before learned claims tribunal and was proceeded ex-parte.

Learned claims tribunal after hearing both the parties and after going through the evidence available on record allowed the claim petition of the appellants - claimants and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.804524/- which was directed to be paid by respondent No. 2 - Driver of the offending vehicle.

Learned counsel for the appellants argued that learned claims tribunal has wrongly fastened the liability on the driver of the offending vehicle against the settled principle of law because registered owner is respondent No. 1 - Manoj.
It is further argued that learned claims tribunal has also awarded the compensation on the lesser side.
Heard and perused the available record.

Learned claims tribunal on the ground that offending vehicle was sold by Manoj to Raghuraj by sale letter Ex.D-3 and, thereafter, by Raghuraj to Ramsiya by sale letter Ex.D-4 held that at the time of accident, respondent No. 1 - Manoj was not the owner of the offending vehicle and fastened the liability on respondent No. 2 - driver of the offending vehicle.

However, above finding is contrary to law because as per Exh. P-9, particular of the registration issued by Registering Authority, Indore,
registered owner of the offending vehicle was Manoj at the time of accident, therefore, merely on the basis of sale letters, it cannot be said that Ramsiya was the owner of the offending vehicle.
Consequently, aforesaid finding of learned claims tribunal is hereby set aside and it is directed that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation jointly and severely.
So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, there is no dispute with regard to the fact that at the time of accident, deceased was 30 years old and was getting Rs.5521/- per month.

In view of the above as well as in the light of the case laws of National Insurance Company vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors.; 2017 ACJ 2700 as well as Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors.; AIR 2009 SC 3104, considering the annual income of the deceased to be Rs.66,252/-, dependency 2/3 (Rs.66252 x 2/3 = 44,168), future prospect @ 50% (44168 x 50/100 =
22084), multiplier of 17 [(44168 + 22084) x 17 = Rs.11,26,284/-), and Rs.70,000/- in other heads,

sentences.text: total compensation amount comes to Rs.11,96,284/-.
As such, the total amount awarded to the claimants is enhanced from Rs.8,04,524/- to Rs.11,96,284/-.

The enhanced amount comes to Rs.3,21,760/- (Rupees Three Lakh Twenty One Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixty only), with interest at the rate as fixed by the tribunal in the award which is directed to be paid to the claimants by the respondents jointly and severely in the same apportionment as directed by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount of compensation Rs.3,21,760/- shall be payable to the claimants within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award impugned passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the claimants within four weeks' from today and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
The appeal is allowed and disposed of in above terms.
